functional: Only the IDO_CHAIRPERSON may act here. An IDO_OFFICER holds REVIEW_REQUEST and can do the first review, but this stage is closed to them — the role check, not the permission, is what separates them.
The final title override is optional and is applied only when non-empty.
Approving requires a signature; the URL is copied onto the request.
Rejecting requires a note and no signature.
Approving sets five things in one transaction: the signature pair, idoFinalStatus, finalDirectorStatus and masterStatus, plus the audit log.
The signature stamped here is printed in the RECOMMENDATION BY IDO block of the PDF — but only once the Director's final approval lands (spec 016).
Once actioned the page opens read-only, showing the signature, the date and the title that was signed.
authorization: Route gate: assertAuthenticatedRoleFn with ['IDO_CHAIRPERSON'] — the narrowest gate in the app.
Server gate: roleProcedure('IDO_CHAIRPERSON') on both procedures, then assertPermission(REVIEW_REQUEST), then the stage check on idoFinalStatus, then the signature check on approval.

An IDO_OFFICER calling idoFinalApprove gets FORBIDDEN from roleProcedure even though they hold REVIEW_REQUEST. This is the test that proves the role gate and the permission gate are doing different jobs.
The stage check reads idoFinalStatus, not masterStatus.
ux: The confirmation dialog states the exact title that will be signed off. A chairperson who typed an override and forgot must see it before committing.
The current title and the override sit next to each other, so the difference is visible without switching pages.
'Approve & Sign' says what it does — this is the moment a signature is attached, not a routine approval.
A missing signature is explained on the page with a link to the profile.
The read-only state after approval shows the signature image and the timestamp, so a returning chairperson sees their own act.

edge_cases: An empty override must not blank finalTitle. Spreading the input straight into the update is the failure — the write has to be conditional on a non-empty value.

This is the only stage where role and permission genuinely diverge: both IDO roles hold REVIEW_REQUEST and only one may act. A refactor that gates on the permission alone silently opens the stage to every officer.

The signature stamped here does not appear on the PDF until finalDirectorStatus is APPROVED. A chairperson who signs and then checks the PDF will see nothing, and the page should say so rather than let them assume the stamp failed.
The override field is lifted to the page so the action button can read it; keeping it inside the form component and passing a stale prop is how an override silently fails to send.
idoFinalStatus is set to UNDER_IDO_FINAL_REVIEW by the DIRECTOR's approval, not here. If that write is ever moved, this stage's guard has nothing to match.

The chairperson also appears at the first review stage (spec 010); the staff dashboard routes on idoFinalStatus to tell the two apart, so a request that reaches this stage must never route back to /review.
out_of_scope: The first IDO review — spec 010, which an officer may also do.
The PDF and its signature gate — spec 016.
Changing anything other than the final title at this stage — the request's content is fixed once it leaves the requestor.
